summary.headline: Laxmi India Finance Q1 FY27: AUM up 27% YoY to ₹1,721 crore, profit ₹16.43 crore (+70%), GNPA 2.08% including a ₹18–19 crore Upmoney exposure.
summary.overview:
Management presented at the GIA BFSI Fintech virtual event on August 20, 2026, reporting Q1 FY27 AUM of ₹1,721 crore (+27% YoY) and disbursements of ₹230 crore (+38%). Profit was ₹16.43 crore (+70%), with ROE 13.86%, ROTA 3.45% and NIM 11.36%. Borrowing cost has fallen to about 10.48% from 11.73% pre-IPO, and management guided to a further 22–25 bps cut this fiscal. The Upmoney exposure (₹18–19 crore, about 70% provided) was the main asset-quality focus; ex-Upmoney GNPA is 0.83%.</overview>

segments.name: Secured MSME / SME
segments.commentary: Largest product, about 80–82% of business along with SME loans; yield 32.48% on June closing. Ticket size ₹6–6.5 lakh; bounce rate ~30%, with ~93–94% of bounced cases closed; PAR 30 ~7%.

segments.name: Vehicle finance (used personal and commercial)
segments.commentary: Yield 19.87%; offered in a limited number of branches, mainly Rajasthan, parts of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. Used-vehicle turnaround 24–48 hours.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of about 28%, with a medium-term target of about 30% CAGR; management said 30% should not be a challenge.
Borrowing cost expected to fall by a further 22–25 bps this financial year; management expects sanctions at 10% or below to lower the overall cost.
Plans to open about 30–35 branches this financial year (196 branches currently); Chhattisgarh to reach 15–20 branches from about 10.
Medium-term ROTA target of about 4% versus 3.45% now, via lower borrowing and operating costs.
Credit cost expected to stay around 1%.
capex_capacity: Branch footprint: 196 branches across six states. Rajasthan 94 locations, Gujarat 24, Madhya Pradesh 44, Uttar Pradesh 14–15, Maharashtra 6–7 (Maharashtra entered in 2026).
Branch break-even in about 7–9 months at AUM of ₹1.5–2 crore; monthly branch cost about ₹1.5–2 lakh.
Cluster model: six branches per cluster, 100–200 km radius; staffing of 5–6 relationship officers per branch (Tier 1 up to 7–10).
Gold loans shelved because they need capex; supply-chain financing put on hold after RBI notices on revolving credit.
About 900 in sales, 200 in collections, 60 in credit, 150 in operations; more than 2,000 employees in total.
demand_pricing: Competition from PSU banks and small finance banks in vehicle finance is seen as limited, since they focus on customers with multiple vehicles and do not finance used vehicles. Management cites doorstep service and tehsil-level presence.
Credit cost of about 1% against 21–22% yield on the core book, per management.
Collections fell to about 89% in September (highest-stress period), recovered to 93.20% in March and are above 92% now.
Upmoney: ~₹18–19 crore exposure, ~70% provided, remainder ~30%; case filed and resolution being pursued.
Post-Upmoney controls: ticket-size restriction, monthly and quarterly data reviews, lending restricted to existing geographies, property papers held in custody.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Upmoney issue and gross NPA with and without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure ~₹18–19 crore, ~70% provided with the remaining ~30% still to be provided; case filed and confident of an outcome in its favour. GNPA 2.08% including Upmoney and 0.83% excluding it.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach 30% CAGR and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is ~28%; new branches in UP and Maharashtra are ramping up. Growth is expected to come mainly from MSME, with vehicle finance in a limited number of branches.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for gold loans, unsecured or top-up loans and new verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: A digital personal-loan product for salaried professionals is in development. A subprime secured MSME product needs only board approval and requires documented income. Gold loans are on hold pending capex capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Co-lending plans and bank funding mix?
qa_highlights.answer: No co-lending arrangement today; a future plan to forward buyout cases to banks. About 80–82% of borrowings come from banks, with 28–29 bank lenders and 50–53 lenders in total. Weighted borrowing tenor about 53 months.

qa_highlights.question: Scope to cut cost of borrowing from ~10.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Further 22–25 bps reduction expected this year. ICICI Bank and City Union Bank onboarded, with more banks in the pipeline; sanctions at 10% or below will lower the blended cost.

risks_watch: Upmoney exposure (~₹18–19 crore, ~30% still unprovided) and the outcome of the legal case.
Bounce rate about 30% and PAR 30 about 7%; the gap to the ~1% credit cost depends on collection efficiency staying above 92%.
Growth in new states (UP, Maharashtra) is early; branch productivity still developing.
RBI draft on NBFC lending and revolving credit: management says no current product is affected, but supply-chain financing is on hold.
Borrowing cost falls depend on new bank sanctions at 10% or below; current pricing is still about 10.48%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, funding cost and secured-lending credit quality, but noticeably defensive on the Upmoney lapse and vague on some figures (for example, the collection-rate history and GNPA quotes were partly unsure). The management also repeatedly deferred to the wider market and RBI context.
key_quotes: Before the IPO, our cost of borrowing was approximately 11.73%. As of now, we are borrowing at approximately 10.48%.
We have guided to approximately 28% growth. That is a strong number because Q1 is a little slow, but we still achieved 28% growth.
